<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2890909aa48b64d91b4b18748b91374f32b4b44` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a9d667e8920a924fb6cde59d4ce7b6c3e0c508ee` — the merge of head `64a75d2bc00f44ca510217d5f8e16f5778f6781d` into base `b2890909aa48b64d91b4b18748b91374f32b4b44`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a9d667e8920a924fb6cde59d4ce7b6c3e0c508ee && git checkout a9d667e8920a924fb6cde59d4ce7b6c3e0c508ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b2890909aa48b64d91b4b18748b91374f32b4b44 64a75d2bc00f44ca510217d5f8e16f5778f6781d && git checkout -B drift-repro b2890909aa48b64d91b4b18748b91374f32b4b44 && git merge --no-ff 64a75d2bc00f44ca510217d5f8e16f5778f6781d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2890909aa48b64d91b4b18748b91374f32b4b44
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e14af57d4d315853c3ba70c26db01810822645a5`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #24822 (body and all 8 comments, including the seat call `6305891812` and the dev reports `6305849709` and `6308104846`), PR #25048 (body and 7 files), and the net diff against `main` from merge base `dfe60e3a0`. Every finding below was read off the code at this head. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Boundary. RIGHT: no pair outside the wall becomes storable.**
- **What the wall is.** The Layer 0 predicate takes four shapes (`tenant-layer.ts` `tenantLayer0FilterOf`): `{organization_id: id}`, `{organization_id: {$in: [...]}}`, the frozen deny sentinel, or `null`. `clearsWall` matches it with `matchesFilterCondition`. There, `$in` and equality use `looseEq`, which is strict `===` with a Date-only exception. So a row clears only when its value is exactly an admitted id string. An array, object or number is refused.
- **Where the value is judged.** The spare happens only where step 3.7 composed the seam with `tenantParts` non-empty. That same block has already run the payload half (`suppliedRows.every(clearsWall)`) before `next()`. The engine then calls the seam's per-row loop (`namesOrganization(row)` and not `clearsWall(row)` refuses) after the static-`readonly` strip. That is before `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` and before the driver.
- **Who can set the seam.** `insert()` builds `opCtx` fresh from `{object, operation, data, options, context}`. So no caller, and no REST door, can supply the seam. Only a registered middleware can.
- **By posture.**
  - `single`: no Layer 0 and no member. Unchanged.
  - `isolated`: {A} before and after. The value is now stored as sent, not stripped and stamped.
  - `group`: the explicit payload on the injected column goes from {A} to {A, C}, which equals the wall's set.
- **Unwall-judged paths.** I found no path where a caller-supplied `organization_id` reaches storage without a wall verdict.
- **Accept-set changes the diff implies that the PR body's two tables do not list:**
  - **F1 (right, unpinned, not in the tables).** Case: under `group`, a member with a non-empty membership set and NO active organization inserts a row naming C, which is in the set.
    - Before: the strip took C, the stored image named no organization, and the `insertLacksActiveOrganization` arm refused 403 (ADR-0123 D2).
    - After: the member is set (an insert, `tenantParts` non-empty), so C stays on the row. `someRowHasNowhereToLand()` is false and the loop admits C. `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` returns `undefined` because every row carries an organization. driver-sql's `injectTenantOnInsert` leaves C in place. Result: refused before, stored as C after. This is read off the code, not measured.
    - Why it is right: ADR-0123's amendment scopes the D2 insert arms to "a row that names no organization". The arm's own comment says a row naming its organization "where the engine keeps a session's value, carries one and lands as before". Naming D is still refused by the payload half.
  - **F2 (right, unpinned).** Case: an on-behalf-of insert (ADR-0090 D10) where the caller crosses the wall (its Layer 0 is `null`) and the delegator is walled. `tenantParts` is the delegator's part alone, so the member is set. The explicit value is then held to the delegator's wall and stored as sent where that wall admits it. Before, it was taken and stamped, or refused under D2. The PR body's operator rows cover only the shape with no delegator.
  - **F3 (right, reporting only).** Case: an ARRAY insert by a walled member with an explicit empty `organization_id` (`null` or empty string). Middleware A fills only non-array payloads, so the empty value reaches the engine.
    - Before: taken, reported, and refused under strict.
    - After: spared, not reported, and not refused under strict.
    - What is stored does not change: driver-sql's `injectTenantOnInsert` fills an empty value from `tenantId`, so the active organization is stored as before.

**(b) Setter. RIGHT.**
- **The one assignment.** `security-plugin.ts:4340` is the only assignment in source. It is a spread conditioned on `operation === 'insert'` and `tenantParts` non-empty, on the new object step 3.7 composes.
- **Where it is not set:**
  - Step 3.6's `newWriteImageCheck()` (`:3818`; installed at `:3831` for an insert and `:3901` for an update) carries no member, and the composition never mutates it.
  - An update seam fails the operation conjunct.
  - The crossing operator's no-active-organization seam has empty `tenantParts`, so the member stays unset.
  - `isSystem` short-circuits the middleware, and the engine also gates on `!isSystem` (`engine.ts:15845`).
- **The private mirror.** `WriteImageCheckSeam` gains the member (`:271`).
- **The engine only reads it.** The engine never sets the member.
- **The delegated case.** F2 sets the member with non-empty `tenantParts`. That is right under the ruled condition, because the loop does judge the row there.

**(c) Engine. RIGHT.**
- **The read.** `wallJudgesOrganization` is `!isSystem` AND `judgesOrganization === true`. It is read once, inside the middleware chain's final handler, so the seam is already in place.
- **Both passes.** The value feeds the pre-hook withhold and the post-hook strip through `insertStaticReadonlySubject`. That helper deletes only `SystemFieldName.ORGANIZATION_ID` from `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`'s `{name, fields}`. It returns `null` when nothing remains, which is the same as a strip with nothing to take.
- **Unchanged:** `rule-validator.ts`; `validate()`, which still calls `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` directly (`engine.ts:15353`); `stripRuntimeOwnedFields`; the update strips; and `tenantLayer0Verdict`.
- **F4 (observation, not named).** The spare is keyed on the column NAME, not on the injected definition.
  - The registry keeps an authored `organization_id`, and "the object stays walled on it". So on a tenancy-enabled object that is not `sys_`, an author-declared `readonly: true` `organization_id` is also spared on walled inserts.
  - This is the same silent-replacement class, and the wall still judges the value.
  - The PR body and changeset describe only the platform-injected column.
  - No in-tree object reaches this: `sys_` objects are outside `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`.

**(d) Pins. RIGHT for the ruled matrix.**
- **organizations, real stack:**
  - `group`: a sister organization stored, single and array; a non-member refused, single and array; an absent value stamped and not reported; strict stores.
  - `isolated`: the equal organization stored and not reported; a different one refused, single and array.
  - The no-wall paths: `single`, `single` with a check, `single` under strict, security plugin absent (both postures), the operator crossing with and without an active organization, and a tenancy-disabled authored column.
  - `isSystem`.
- **plugin-security:** the member is SET for `isolated`, for `group` single and array, and when composed with a check. It is UNSET on the `single` check seam, the operator's no-organization seam and an update seam. There is no seam for an operator with an active organization, or for a system context.
- **objectql:** set, absent, `false` and no seam; `created_by` is still taken; strict; `isSystem`; `validate()`.
- **Ablations.** A1 through A6 are in the PR body, each with a predicted direction and the red counts observed. The `operation === 'insert'` conjunct was not ablated. The update pin asserts the member directly, and no engine path reads it on an update today.
- **Gaps:** F1 and F2 have no pin.
- **Nit:** the PR body's A1 row reads `org 1 failed / 39`. The dev report reads `/ 40`.

**(e) Public surface. The two named changes are right and declared, but the list is incomplete.**
- **Named and declared:** the optional `PostHookWriteImageCheck.judgesOrganization`, and strict changing from refusing to storing for an admitted organization.
- **Also implied by the diff:**
  - an admitted organization is no longer reported through `droppedFields`, the readonly WARN or `onFieldsDropped` (named in the changeset);
  - F1's change from refused to stored;
  - `beforeInsert` hooks now see the caller's `organization_id` on walled inserts (named in the PR body's pins, not in the changeset);
  - F4;
  - F3.
- **Effect on the declaration:** every one of these widens, none moves a pair outside the wall, and none changes the level.

### ② Semver level

- **The changeset** (`.changeset/24822-wall-judged-organization-stored.md`) declares `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`. It MATCHES what the diff publishes:
  - `objectql` is `minor`: an additive optional member on an exported published interface, plus strict changing from refusing to storing. The precedent is the `tenantLayer0Verdict` CHANGELOG entry.
  - `plugin-security` is `patch`: it changes a private type and its own seam composition.
- **Packaging:** neither package is private. Both are in the `fixed` group, so the line moves minor regardless.
- **Version skew:** either package upgraded alone is inert. An older engine ignores the member. A newer engine without the setter strips as before.
- **Clause-②:** `yes (widening)` sits at line start in both the PR body and the changeset. RIGHT: I found no narrowing, meaning nothing accepted today is refused after this change.
- **Card link:** the PR is `Part of #24822`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev questions.** Round 2 had no `open_questions`. Round 1's Q1 and Q2 were answered A in `6305891812`, and the diff implements A:
  - the member, and step 3.7 as its only setter;
  - both passes;
  - `validate()` untouched;
  - the `isolated`-equal pin rewritten, and its `single` twin kept.
- **Ruled premise.** The premise holds by reading.
- **Deviations.**
  - A1 was applied at step 3.6's seam creation (`:3831`). That is right: the check-only seam is step 3.6's object.
  - The census row sits inside the claim.
  - The trailer deviation is outside this record.
- **The Acceptance-notes finding (the wall-blind `validate` preview).**
  - Introduced in part. The preview was wall-blind before this PR: for a row naming D, it answered `valid: true` with a drop while the write refused 403, before and after.
  - What this PR adds is one false report. For a walled insert naming an admitted organization, the preview still lists `organization_id` as dropped while the write stores it. `ValidateDataResponse` says "fields the write would LEGALLY strip", so that is false for this cell, where before the preview and the write agreed.
  - It does not block. The preview runs no middleware by design, and the engine doc already calls it "not a promise the write would succeed". Agreement would need the wall's verdict in the preview: either a mirror, which is the re-derivation the #15706 ruling removed, or a preview that runs the middleware. Both are outside this claim.
  - It is pinned (objectql file) and carried in the Acceptance notes with dedupe words.
  - ESCALATED to the seat at ACCEPT: file it to fix the preview, or to state the limit in `ValidateDataResponse`.
- **F1 and F2.** ESCALATED to the seat at ACCEPT. They need pins:
  - `group`, no active organization: naming C stores C; naming D is refused 403; naming none gets the D2 refusal;
  - the delegated crossing operator.

  They also need a row in the boundary table, in this PR or as half 2's first pins. They do not block: each is admitted by the wall and matches ADR-0123's amended scope.
- **F4.** ESCALATED to the seat. Either name the spare of an authored read-only column in the changeset, or narrow the spare to the injected definition. Decide before half 2, where an authored `readonly` `organization_id` on UPDATE reads as an intent to make it immutable.
- **What half 2 (UPDATE) must not regress:**
  1. The setter stays conditional on non-empty `tenantParts`. It must never be set on the step 3.6 check seam or the crossing operator's seam. Replace the `operation === 'insert'` conjunct deliberately; do not just delete it.
  2. Step 3.7 composes no wall seam for an ARRAY update payload, so the update strip must not spare the column there.
  3. Keep #22278's refusal of an emptied organization on both halves, and the payload-half refusal of D.
  4. Spare on the by-id seam (`engine.ts` near `:18223`) and the predicate seam (near `:18526`) from ONE read, as this PR does, so the hook view and the stored row agree. Keep `isSystem` and update-mode `validate()` as they are. Add the census row.
  5. Keep the `honoured` fail-closed guard.
  6. Rewrite step 3.7's comment "For UPDATE this makes `organization_id` effectively immutable" once re-points under `group` are stored.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-10-21T04:45Z.**
  - 40 runs: 29 `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 failed.
  - Skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance.
  - Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, every Lint and Type Check lane, Build Core, Test Core (1/6) and Test Core (5/6).
  - **pending:** Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6), Test Core (6/6).
  - This PASS rests on the gates read so far. A red Test Core voids it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `64a75d2bc00f44ca510217d5f8e16f5778f6781d`
Local-runs: probe — one `git merge-tree` of this head against `origin/main` `72518d20f`, to answer the main-moved question; it wrote only unreferenced objects (no ref, checkout, build, test or gate run), and the disjoint file lists answer the same question without it

**Inputs read.** Card #24822: its body and all 11 comments, through `6309258045`. PR #25048: its body, its 7-file list, and the net diff against merge base `b2890909a`, which is the PR's base. The code the hunks cite, at the head. The head's check-runs, read last. Record rendered 2026-10-21T06:19Z.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) RIGHT: the storable `(caller, organization)` pairs equal the Layer 0 wall's admitted set, before and after, on every posture.**
- **When the engine spares the column.** Only when `opCtx.postHookWriteImageCheck?.judgesOrganization === true` and the context is not system (`engine.ts` :15908).
- **Who sets the member.** Only step 3.7's composed seam (`security-plugin.ts` :4346).
- **What that seam judges.** Its `evaluate` holds every live row that names an organization to `clearsWall` (:4325), which is every `tenantParts` filter (:4139).
- **When it runs.** After the hooks, and before `resolveSystemInsertOrganization`, encryption, autonumbers and the driver (`engine.ts` :16445).
- **The payload half.** `suppliedRows.every(clearsWall)` (:4230) has already refused every supplied value outside the wall, before the engine runs.
- **So with the member set, every stored organization is one `clearsWall` admitted.**
  - `clearsWall` is `matchesFilterCondition` over `{ organization_id: A }` or `{ organization_id: { $in: set } }`.
  - Its `looseEq` is strict for anything but a Date. So a number, an array or an object in `organization_id` counts as naming an organization, and it is refused, never admitted.
- **What reaches storage unjudged: only `null`, `''` or an absent key** (`namesOrganization` is false for these).
  - driver-sql's `injectTenantOnInsert` (:15839, shared by driver-turso) fills all three from `tenantId`, so the active organization is stored. That is F3.
  - With no active organization, the ADR-0123 D2 arm refuses the row.
  - The memory and mongodb drivers refuse tenant-scoped calls outright.
  - **No path found where a caller-chosen organization reaches storage without a wall verdict.**
- **Per posture:**
  - `single` composes no Layer 0, so `tenantParts` is empty, the member is never set, and the strip runs as before.
  - `isolated`: {A} before and {A} after.
  - `group`: an explicit payload on the injected column goes from {A} to {A, C}, which is exactly the Layer 0 `$in` set. Declared-column objects and hook-placed values were already {A, C}.
- **Paths with no member, unchanged:**
  - step 3.6's business-check seam (:3837, :3907);
  - the crossing operator's seam with no wall parts;
  - every update seam;
  - `isSystem`: the middleware returns before step 3.6 (:2451), and the engine strips nothing for it;
  - a stack without plugin-security;
  - a context with no `userId` (step 3.7's own gate, :3995).

**(b) RIGHT: `judgesOrganization` is set only on step 3.7's insert seam, and only when `tenantParts` is non-empty.**
- **One assignment in the tree outside tests,** inside the composition that runs when `tenantParts` is non-empty or the operator has no active organization: `...(opCtx.operation === 'insert' && tenantParts.length ... ? { judgesOrganization: true } : {})` (:4346).
- **The engine only reads it** (:15909).
- **The private `WriteImageCheckSeam` type** gains the optional member. It is not exported.
- **Never set on:**
  - step 3.6's `newWriteImageCheck()` seams, for insert (:3837) and update (:3907);
  - the operator's no-active-organization seam with no parts, where the spread is `{}`;
  - any update (the `operation` conjunct);
  - `isSystem`, which never reaches steps 3.6 and 3.7.
- **`tenantParts` is not reassigned** after the composition.
- **The delegator-only case sets it, rightly.** Take a crossing operator (its own Layer 0 is `null`) acting for a walled delegator. The parts are then the delegator's wall alone, and that is the composed admitted set: `intersectTenantLayer0Verdicts` turns `none` on one side into the other side. This is F2.

**(c) RIGHT: the engine's spare.**
- **One read, one helper.** `wallJudgesOrganization` is read once (:15908) and passed to ONE helper, `insertStaticReadonlySubject` (:2414).
- **Both passes use the helper:** the pre-hook withhold (:2509) and the post-hook strip (:16346). Both read `this._registry.getObject(object)`, so the hook view and the stored row cannot disagree.
- **What it removes:** `organization_id` only, and only when the member is set AND `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(schema, organization_id) !== 'author'`.
  - Otherwise it returns the subject unmodified.
  - When it does remove the column, it rebuilds the whole `{ name, fields }` shape that `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` returns.
  - Other read-only keys stay judged; `created_by` is pinned.
- **`validate()` is unchanged.** It still calls `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` directly (:15417), and `rule-validator.ts` is untouched.
- **The `!isSystem` conjunct is an equivalent mutant.** The strips never run for `isSystem`, so no ablation can turn it red. It is defence in depth, not a gap in the pins.

**(d) RIGHT: the pins cover the ruled matrix.**
- **organizations, real stack:**
  - `group`: C single and array, D single and array, none, and strict C;
  - `isolated`: A single (the rewritten #21682 cell) and array, another organization single and array, and F3's `null` / `''`;
  - F1: C single and array, D, and none;
  - F4;
  - the no-wall paths:
    - `single` without the runtime, with a business check, and under strict;
    - `group` and `isolated` without plugin-security, both the taken value and the unreported stamp;
    - the crossing operator under both postures;
    - the operator with no active organization;
    - the tenancy-disabled authored column;
    - the system context.
- **plugin-security:**
  - the member SET or UNSET on each seam;
  - no seam for an operator with an active organization, or for the system context;
  - F2, on a delegator rebuilt from stored rows.
- **objectql:**
  - the member set, absent, `false`, and no seam at all;
  - strict;
  - another read-only key;
  - F4;
  - the system context;
  - `validate()`.
- **The negative pins are ablation-verified, per the PR body:**
  - A1, the business-check seam;
  - A2, the operator seam;
  - A4, every no-wall cell. Its org count of 10 / 40 is consistent with the ten no-wall cells that carry a value;
  - R3B, the D2 arm;
  - R4, F4 alone.
- **The refusals and the positive controls are ablated too:** refusals by A3 and R3A; positive controls by A6 and R3C.

**(e) As the brief words it, two items as the ONLY public-surface changes, the list is WRONG. The PR's own list is RIGHT.**
- **The diff implies more than the member and strict:**
  - the headline change: an admitted organization is stored as sent;
  - an admitted value is no longer reported (no `droppedFields`, no `onFieldsDropped`, no read-only WARN);
  - `beforeInsert` sees the caller's value;
  - F1: a 403 becomes a stored row;
  - F2;
  - F3;
  - F4's boundary.
- **All of them are in the PR body's `## Public surface` and in the changeset.**
- **How the member is published:** through the exported `OperationContext` type (`index.ts` :159), which is the reach the changeset names.
- **Nothing is missing.** Two precision notes are in ③ (N1, N2).

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/objectql` `minor`: RIGHT.** An optional member is added to a published type, and the strict flag widens. `Clause-②: yes` requires at least minor.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`: RIGHT.** The type it changes is private, and the change is a fix; nothing it publishes moves.
  - Each package degrades safely without the other's new version: an older engine ignores the member, and an older plugin never sets it.
- **`@objectstack/organizations`: RIGHT.** Its diff is tests only, so no changeset is owed.
- **The `Clause-②` line: RIGHT.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands at line start in both the PR body and the changeset, as the same sentence.
  - There is no narrowing arm: nothing the engine's own gates accepted is refused now. N2 covers outcomes that depend on stored state.
  - `Check Changeset` is green.
- **Tier: RIGHT.** None of the 7 paths is a published schema or a governed path, so the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT` is the right tier.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The earlier review's escalations, judged again on this head:**
- **F1, `group` with no active organization:** inside the admitted set.
  - C is stored only where C is in `accessible_org_ids`, the context's Layer 0 `$in`.
  - D is still the wall's 403 (R3A). Naming none still meets the D2 arm (R3B).
  - This matches ADR-0123's amended scope: its insert arms refuse a row "that names no organization".
- **F2, a crossing operator acting for a walled delegator:** inside the admitted set.
  - C is stored only where the delegator's wall admits it.
  - D, and C under `isolated`, are refused (R3A, sec 2 / 12).
- **F3, an array row's `null` / `''`:** inside the admitted set. The value is not judged, the active organization is stamped, and strict no longer refuses it.
- **F4, an authored `readonly: true` `organization_id`:**
